title: Hardness of Vertex Splitting: Cographs, Chordal Graphs, and Beyond
summary: Vertex splitting replaces a vertex (v) by two nonadjacent vertices whose neighborhoods together equal (N(v)). A split is \emph{exclusive} if these neighborhoods are disjoint and \emph{shallow} if no newly created vertex is split again. For a graph property (Π), \textsc{(Π)-Vertex Splitting} asks whether at most (k) splits can transform a graph (G) into one satisfying (Π). We continue the systematic study of this operation and settle several open problems.
